BAJAJ ELECTRICALS : SHEKHAR BAJAJ TO BECOME CHAIRMAN EMERITUS, SAMPATHKUMAR NAMED NON-EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN

• Shekhar Bajaj to transition out as Executive Chairman effective 31 Dec 2026; becomes Non-Executive Director and Chairman Emeritus from 1 Jan 2027, subject to shareholder approval
• Sudarshan Sampathkumar, currently an Independent Director, appointed Non-Executive Chairman effective 1 Jan 2027, subject to shareholder approval
• Sanjay Sachdeva continues as Managing Director and CEO; MD will lead and run the company while the Non-Executive Chairman leads the Board
• New model provides clear separation between executive management and Board leadership for governance, performance oversight, succession and risk
• Bajaj family remains long-term promoter and shareholder; Shekhar Bajaj, Pooja Bajaj and Nirav Bajaj continue to serve on the Board
Impact: Neutral (Governance restructuring with management continuity; succession and oversight roles formally split, no change to MD/CEO leadership)

DCM SHRIRAM LTD Q2 CONCALL: RENEWABLE POWER TARGET OF ONE-THIRD OF TOTAL REQUIREMENTS, 70–80 MW ADDITIONAL CAPACITY PLANNED, DEMERGER PROGRESS TARGETED AROUND Q1 FY28 & NEW CHEMICAL CAPACITY RAMP-UP

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS RENEWABLE ENERGY TO CONTRIBUTE APPROXIMATELY ONE-THIRD OF TOTAL POWER REQUIREMENTS OVER THE NEXT YEAR, SUPPORTING LOWER ENERGY COSTS & IMPROVED COMPETITIVENESS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS RETURNS ABOVE APPROXIMATELY 20–25% ON RENEWABLE POWER INVESTMENTS, SUPPORTED BY SAVINGS AGAINST CONVENTIONAL ENERGY COSTS

• MANAGEMENT CLARIFIED THAT Q1 FY28 REPRESENTS AN INTENDED TIMELINE FOR PROGRESSING THE DEMERGER SCHEME, NOT A CONFIRMED COMPLETION DATE

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS CHEMICALS PROFITABILITY TO BENEFIT OVER TIME FROM HIGHER CAPACITY UTILIZATION, DOWNSTREAM INTEGRATION, COST OPTIMIZATION & NEW PROJECT RAMP-UP

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS APPROXIMATELY 45% CAPTIVE CHLORINE CONSUMPTION AT BHARUCH & 62% AT KOTA AFTER RELEVANT DOWNSTREAM PROJECTS ARE COMMISSIONED

• INCLUDING PIPELINE-LINKED CUSTOMERS, MANAGEMENT EXPECTS APPROXIMATELY 70% OF BHARUCH CHLORINE OUTPUT TO BE CAPTIVELY CONSUMED OR LINKED TO DIRECT CUSTOMERS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS STRONGER CHLORINE INTEGRATION TO REDUCE EXPOSURE TO NEGATIVE CHLORINE REALIZATIONS & SUPPORT MORE STABLE CAUSTIC SODA ECONOMICS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS CAUSTIC SODA OPERATIONS TO BENEFIT FROM DOWNSTREAM DEMAND, EXPORT OPPORTUNITIES & HIGHER PLANT UTILIZATION, SUBJECT TO MARKET PRICES

• MANAGEMENT CAUTIONED THAT PVC PROFITABILITY REMAINS HIGHLY SENSITIVE TO FUEL COSTS, WITH ENERGY ACCOUNTING FOR APPROXIMATELY 60–70% OF PRODUCTION COSTS

• MANAGEMENT PLANS TO OPTIMIZE ETHANOL FEEDSTOCK MIX, INCLUDING GREATER USE OF FCI RICE WHERE AVAILABLE, TO ADDRESS PRESSURE ON MAIZE-BASED ETHANOL ECONOMICS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS MAIZE-BASED ETHANOL MARGINS TO REMAIN UNDER PRESSURE DUE TO HIGHER FEEDSTOCK COSTS & LOWER PROCUREMENT REALIZATIONS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS SUGAR OPERATIONS TO REMAIN DEPENDENT ON CANE AVAILABILITY, RECOVERY RATES & WEATHER CONDITIONS, WITHOUT PROVIDING NUMERICAL PRODUCTION GUIDANCE

• MANAGEMENT CONFIRMED PHASE 1 OF THE KOTA ALUMINIUM EXTRUSION FACILITY HAS BEEN COMMISSIONED, WHILE PHASE 2 DEVELOPMENT IS PROGRESSING

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS A POSSIBLE PARTIAL RECOVERY IN SHRIRAM FARM SOLUTIONS SALES DURING Q3 FY27, DEPENDING ON CROP CONDITIONS & CHANNEL DEMAND

• MANAGEMENT DID NOT PROVIDE NUMERICAL FY27 OR FY28 REVENUE, EBITDA, PBDIT OR PAT GUIDANCE

• MANAGEMENT DID NOT ENDORSE THE SUGGESTED FY28 REVENUE TARGET OF ₹20,000 CR DURING THE ANALYST DISCUSSION

ECOBOARD : SUSPENDS ECO BUILD OPERATIONS FOR ONE YEAR

• Board approved temporary suspension of manufacturing at Particle Board Build Division (Eco Build) for one year with immediate effect
• Eco Build contributed ₹15.33 Cr turnover, 64.14% of company turnover in FY2025-26, with net worth of ₹9.14 Cr
• Suspension due to sustained operating losses, non-availability of raw material and capex needed for refurbishment without assurance of viable operations
• No sale of the division involved; no binding agreement for sale entered into as on date
• Company to reallocate financial, technical and managerial resources to Energy Division (Eco Energy) - ETP services and CBG plant execution
• Rama Krishna Raju Gottumukkala resigned as CEO, continues as MD; Venkatraman Krishnamurthi appointed CEO with effect from October 28, 2026
Impact: Negative (Division generating nearly two-thirds of turnover halted for a year with no resumption timeline, leaving earnings dependent on the smaller Eco Energy business)

• H1 FY27 REVENUE GREW 40% YOY, EBITDA INCREASED 29% & PAT GREW 10%, SUPPORTED BY DIVERSIFICATION & OPERATIONAL IMPROVEMENTS

• VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS CONTRIBUTED APPROXIMATELY 64% OF CONSOLIDATED SALES, REFLECTING MANAGEMENT'S STRATEGY OF SHIFTING TOWARD HIGHER-MARGIN RECYCLING PRODUCTS

• LEAD RECYCLING VOLUMES DECLINED APPROXIMATELY 11% YOY, PRIMARILY DUE TO SCRAP SOURCING DISRUPTIONS LINKED TO WEST ASIA GEOPOLITICAL TENSIONS

• MANAGEMENT CLARIFIED THAT LEAD VOLUME WEAKNESS WAS CAUSED BY RAW MATERIAL SHORTAGES RATHER THAN WEAK END-MARKET DEMAND

• LEAD SCRAP PROCUREMENT HAS AN APPROXIMATELY 80–90-DAY CYCLE, MEANING NEW SOURCING CONTRACTS REQUIRE TIME TO TRANSLATE INTO ACTUAL PLANT SUPPLIES

• Q2 COPPER EBITDA REACHED APPROXIMATELY ₹84.67/KG, SUPPORTED BY SPECIALISED PRODUCT ORDERS, FAVOURABLE RAW MATERIAL MIX & OPERATING EFFICIENCIES

• MANAGEMENT CAUTIONED THAT Q2 COPPER PROFITABILITY WAS EXCEPTIONALLY STRONG & SHOULD NOT BE CONSIDERED THE SUSTAINABLE NEAR-TERM RUN RATE

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS COPPER BACKWARD INTEGRATION THROUGH OWN RECYCLING FACILITIES TO SUPPORT HIGHER SUSTAINABLE EBITDA PER KG OVER THE NEXT 2–3 YEARS

• COMPANY PLANS 29,400 MTPA COPPER RECYCLING CAPACITY AT MANDVI, GUJARAT, WITH ESTIMATED CAPEX OF ₹160 CR & COMMISSIONING TARGETED WITHIN 12 MONTHS

• COMPANY PLANS ADDITIONAL 59,200 MTPA COPPER RECYCLING CAPACITY AT MUNDRA, GUJARAT, WITH ESTIMATED CAPEX OF ₹64 CR & PHASED COMMISSIONING BY MARCH 2029

• BOTH COPPER EXPANSION PROJECTS ARE EXPECTED TO BE FUNDED THROUGH INTERNAL ACCRUALS, SUPPORTING CAPACITY GROWTH WITHOUT DEDICATED EXTERNAL PROJECT FUNDING

• MANAGEMENT UPGRADED FY27 PRESTIGE & ABOVE (P&A) VOLUME GROWTH GUIDANCE TO 30%, SUPPORTED BY STRONG PREMIUMIZATION, VODKA DEMAND, NEW PRODUCT LAUNCHES & IMPROVED DISTRIBUTION

• MANAGEMENT MAINTAINS FY27 EBITDA MARGIN GUIDANCE OF APPROXIMATELY 20%, SUPPORTED BY HIGHER PREMIUM PRODUCT CONTRIBUTION, BETTER REALISATIONS & OPERATING EFFICIENCIES

• MANAGEMENT MAINTAINS FY27 LUXURY PORTFOLIO REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE OF 25%, DRIVEN BY RAMPUR, ROYAL RANTHAMBORE, VIRASAT & OTHER HIGH-VALUE SPIRITS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS VODKA, PARTICULARLY FLAVOURED VODKA, TO OUTPERFORM OTHER SPIRITS CATEGORIES OVER THE NEXT 3–5 YEARS, SUPPORTED BY CHANGING CONSUMER PREFERENCES & CATEGORY EXPANSION

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS REGULAR PORTFOLIO VOLUMES TO STABILISE, WITH POTENTIAL GROWTH OF APPROXIMATELY 1–2%, FOLLOWING RECENT DECLINES CAUSED BY BASE EFFECTS & STATE POLICY CHANGES

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS WORKING CAPITAL TO NORMALISE DURING H2 FY27 AS INVENTORY REQUIREMENTS STABILISE, WHILE GRAIN PRICES COULD BEGIN STABILISING FROM NOVEMBER 2026

• Q2 REVENUE REACHED A RECORD ₹1,746 CR, SUPPORTED BY STRONG PREMIUM SPIRITS DEMAND, HIGHER REALISATIONS & RAPID GROWTH IN VODKA AND LUXURY BRANDS

• Q2 EBITDA REACHED ₹356 CR, WITH EBITDA MARGIN EXPANDING 462 BPS YOY TO 20.4%, REFLECTING SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT IN PRODUCT MIX & OPERATING PROFITABILITY

• Q2 GROSS MARGIN IMPROVED 440 BPS YOY TO 48%, ALTHOUGH IT DECLINED 109 BPS SEQUENTIALLY DUE TO HIGHER RAW MATERIAL & PACKAGING COSTS

• PREMIUM PRODUCT MIX CONTRIBUTED APPROXIMATELY 510 BPS TO REALISATION IMPROVEMENT, WHILE PRICING ACTIONS ADDED AROUND 85 BPS, PARTLY OFFSET BY INPUT-COST INFLATION

• TOTAL IMFL SALES VOLUMES EXCEEDED 10 MILLION CASES, GROWING APPROXIMATELY 7% YOY, WHILE PREMIUM CATEGORIES SIGNIFICANTLY OUTPERFORMED THE OVERALL PORTFOLIO

• PRESTIGE & ABOVE VOLUMES SURGED 36% YOY TO 5.28 MILLION CASES, REFLECTING STRONG PREMIUMIZATION & HIGHER CONSUMER DEMAND FOR VALUE-ADDED SPIRITS

• VODKA PORTFOLIO VOLUMES GREW APPROXIMATELY 49% YOY, WHILE NON-VODKA PREMIUM BRANDS DELIVERED GROWTH OF AROUND 20% OR MORE

• REGULAR SEGMENT VOLUMES DECLINED APPROXIMATELY 15% YOY, AFFECTED BY PREVIOUS-YEAR BASE EFFECTS & CHANGES IN STATE DISTRIBUTION POLICIES

• MANAGEMENT INDICATED VODKA'S SHARE OF INDIA'S IMFL MARKET INCREASED FROM 3.7% IN 2025 TO 4.5% IN 2026 & APPROXIMATELY 6.3% IN Q2 FY27, HIGHLIGHTING STRONG CATEGORY MOMENTUM

• VODKA CONTRIBUTES APPROXIMATELY 30% OF RADICO'S VOLUMES, WHILE FLAVOURED VODKA ACCOUNTS FOR AROUND 75% OF ITS VODKA PORTFOLIO

• MAGIC MOMENTS CONTINUES TO BENEFIT FROM FLAVOURED VODKA DEMAND, WITH JAMUN RECEIVING A POSITIVE RESPONSE & NEW AAM PANNA FLAVOUR SHOWING ENCOURAGING INITIAL TRACTION

• MANAGEMENT ESTIMATES EVERY ADDITIONAL 1 PERCENTAGE POINT OF VODKA MARKET SHARE COULD ADD APPROXIMATELY 4–4.5 MILLION CASES TO THE OVERALL INDIAN VODKA CATEGORY

• AFTER DARK WHISKY GREW APPROXIMATELY 60% IN THE PREVIOUS YEAR, WITH REDESIGNED PACKAGING ALREADY INTRODUCED ACROSS 10 STATES & FURTHER EXPANSION PLANNED

• 8PM PREMIUM BLACK IS SHOWING IMPROVED MOMENTUM FOLLOWING ITS PACKAGING REFRESH, SUPPORTING GROWTH IN THE COMPANY'S BROADER PREMIUM WHISKY PORTFOLIO

• VIRASAT INDIAN SINGLE MALT HAS RECEIVED ENCOURAGING INITIAL DEMAND, TARGETING THE AFFORDABLE-LUXURY SEGMENT WITH PRICING OF APPROXIMATELY ₹3,500–4,000 PER BOTTLE

• LUXURY PORTFOLIO GENERATED APPROXIMATELY ₹475 CR REVENUE IN FY26, WITH MANAGEMENT EXPECTING CONTINUED GROWTH FROM RAMPUR, ROYAL RANTHAMBORE, VIRASAT & PREMIUM GIN

• KARNATAKA PREMIUM VOLUMES GREW OVER 100% DURING Q2, BENEFITING FROM DUTY REDUCTIONS & GREATER PRICING FLEXIBILITY, WHILE THE STATE CONTRIBUTES ONLY APPROXIMATELY 6% OF TOTAL BUSINESS

• MAHARASHTRA P&A PORTFOLIO RETURNED TO GROWTH, WHILE TAMIL NADU VOLUMES INCREASED APPROXIMATELY 20%, SUPPORTED BY IMPROVING MARKET CONDITIONS

SIYARAM SILK MILLS Q2 CONCALL: MANAGEMENT RAISES FY27 REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE TO 14–15%, TARGETS ₹160 CR RETAIL REVENUE, 70 STORES BY FY27-END & ₹100 CR CAPEX

• MANAGEMENT RAISES FY27 REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE TO 14–15%, SUPPORTED BY STRONG FABRIC DEMAND, FESTIVE & WEDDING-SEASON SALES AND EXPANDING RETAIL OPERATIONS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS STRONGER FESTIVE & WEDDING-SEASON DEMAND IN Q3 FY27, PARTICULARLY ACROSS TIER 2 & TIER 3 MARKETS, SUPPORTING FABRIC & APPAREL SALES

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS APPROXIMATELY ₹160 CR RETAIL REVENUE IN FY27, WITH ZCODE & DEVO EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE AROUND 5–7% OF TOTAL COMPANY TURNOVER

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS 70 OPERATIONAL RETAIL STORES BY FY27-END, UP FROM 61 CURRENTLY, WITH FUTURE EXPANSION PRIMARILY LED BY ZCODE

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS DEVO STORE COUNT TO STABILIZE AROUND 20–25, WHILE ZCODE EXPANSION CONTINUES ACROSS SOUTHERN INDIA

• MANAGEMENT MAINTAINS APPROXIMATELY 14% UNDERLYING EBITDA MARGIN REFERENCE, WITH RETAIL EXPANSION EXPECTED TO CREATE A MAXIMUM MARGIN DRAG OF AROUND 150 BPS

• MANAGEMENT PLANS FY27 CAPITAL EXPENDITURE OF APPROXIMATELY ₹100 CR, INCLUDING ₹40–50 CR TOWARD RETAIL EXPANSION, FUNDED THROUGH INTERNAL ACCRUALS

• MANAGEMENT HAS IMPLEMENTED CUMULATIVE SELLING-PRICE INCREASES OF APPROXIMATELY 4–6% OVER THE PAST SIX MONTHS TO PARTIALLY OFFSET RISING RAW MATERIAL COSTS

• Q2 TOTAL INCOME GREW 15.1% YOY TO ₹827 CR, WHILE H1 FY27 TOTAL INCOME INCREASED 15.6% TO ₹1,293 CR

• Q2 EBITDA ROSE 8.3% YOY TO ₹131 CR, WITH EBITDA MARGIN AT APPROXIMATELY 15.8%, REFLECTING CONTINUED INPUT-COST PRESSURES

• Q2 PAT DECLINED 13.8% YOY TO ₹75 CR FROM ₹87 CR, PARTLY DUE TO A ₹24 CR NON-RECURRING OTHER-INCOME ITEM IN THE PRIOR-YEAR QUARTER

• H1 FY27 EBITDA STOOD AT ₹170 CR, WHILE PAT REACHED ₹86 CR, WITH DEBT-TO-EQUITY AT 0.58X

• FABRICS CONTRIBUTED APPROXIMATELY 77% OF Q2 REVENUE, FOLLOWED BY GARMENTS AT 16% & YARN AND OTHER SEGMENTS AT 7%

• FABRIC BUSINESS RECORDED APPROXIMATELY 2.5% VOLUME GROWTH & 11% VALUE GROWTH, SUPPORTED BY BETTER PRODUCT MIX & IMPROVING DEMAND

• RETAIL NETWORK EXPANDED TO 61 OPERATIONAL STORES, COMPRISING 38 ZCODE STORES & 23 DEVO STORES

• H1 FY27 RETAIL REVENUE REACHED APPROXIMATELY ₹65 CR, WITH MANAGEMENT TARGETING A SIGNIFICANTLY STRONGER H2 TO ACHIEVE ITS ₹160 CR FULL-YEAR OBJECTIVE

• MANAGEMENT INDICATED SOME RETAIL STORES HAVE ALREADY ACHIEVED STORE-LEVEL EBITDA PROFITABILITY, WHILE NEW STORE INVESTMENTS CONTINUE TO WEIGH ON OVERALL MARGINS

• RETAIL EXPANSION REQUIRES APPROXIMATELY ₹1–1.5 CR PER STORE IN CAPEX & DEPOSITS, ALONG WITH ₹70–80 LAKH IN INVENTORY INVESTMENT

• H1 FY27 CAPEX STOOD AT APPROXIMATELY ₹51 CR, WITH MANAGEMENT EXPECTING FULL-YEAR SPENDING TO REMAIN WITHIN ITS ₹100 CR PLAN

• MANAGEMENT PLANS TO ANNOUNCE FY28 RETAIL STORE EXPANSION & FUNDING GUIDANCE TOWARD THE END OF FY27, AFTER ASSESSING EXISTING STORE PERFORMANCE

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS PREFERENCE-SHARE LISTING APPROVAL TO TAKE AT LEAST ANOTHER SIX MONTHS, WITH APPLICATIONS ALREADY SUBMITTED TO BSE & NSE

• COMPANY DECLARED AN INTERIM DIVIDEND OF ₹4 PER SHARE, WHILE CONTINUING TO FUND RETAIL EXPANSION THROUGH INTERNAL CASH GENERATION

• MANAGEMENT REMAINS POSITIVE ON FY27 REVENUE GROWTH, FESTIVE DEMAND, FABRIC SALES & RETAIL EXPANSION, BUT RAW MATERIAL INFLATION, RETAIL PROFITABILITY, COMPETITION & MARGIN PRESSURE REMAIN KEY RISKS

UNIMECH AEROSPACE Q2 CONCALL: REVENUE SURGES 98% YOY, PAT JUMPS 103%, ORDER BOOK SOARS 715% TO ₹855 CR, EBITDA MARGIN HITS 40% & GLOBAL AEROSPACE CONTRACTS DRIVE MULTI-YEAR GROWTH

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS H2 FY27 REVENUE TO EXCEED H1 FY27 LEVELS OF ₹231 CR, SUPPORTED BY STRONG AEROSPACE TOOLING DEMAND, PRECISION COMPONENTS, HOBEL BELLOWS & SEMICONDUCTOR BUSINESS RAMP-UP

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS H2 FY27 EBITDA MARGINS TO REMAIN BROADLY SIMILAR TO H1 LEVELS OF APPROXIMATELY 38%, DESPITE INCREASING CONTRIBUTION FROM PRECISION COMPONENTS & NEW PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

• MANAGEMENT MAINTAINS LONG-TERM REVENUE ASPIRATION OF ₹1,000 CR, SUPPORTED BY EXISTING & PLANNED MANUFACTURING CAPACITY, GLOBAL OEM CONTRACTS & EXPANSION INTO SEMICONDUCTORS, NUCLEAR & DEFENCE, WITHOUT A FIXED ACHIEVEMENT TIMELINE

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS OVER 590 QUALIFIED PRECISION COMPONENT PARTS BY FY27-END VS MORE THAN 250 CURRENTLY QUALIFIED, WITH APPROXIMATELY 60–70% OF QUALIFIED PARTS EXPECTED TO ENTER SERIAL PRODUCTION

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS SIGNIFICANT PRECISION COMPONENT SERIAL PRODUCTION SCALE-UP FROM FY28, WITH LONG-TERM REVENUE MIX POTENTIALLY SHIFTING TOWARD 50% TOOLING & 50% PRECISION COMPONENTS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS SEMICONDUCTOR REVENUE TO INCREASE MEANINGFULLY IN H2 FY27 & FY28, WITH 60 PARTS ALREADY QUALIFIED & ANOTHER 20 TARGETED BY DECEMBER 2026

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS WORKING CAPITAL CYCLE TO INCREASE TO APPROXIMATELY 150–160 DAYS BY FY27-END VS 110 DAYS CURRENTLY, REFLECTING HIGHER INVENTORY, CUSTOMER QUALIFICATIONS & PRODUCTION RAMP-UP

• Q2 REVENUE SURGED 98% YOY & 14% QOQ TO ₹123 CR, WHILE NET PROFIT JUMPED 103% YOY TO ₹32 CR

• Q2 EBITDA MARGIN REACHED APPROXIMATELY 40%, WITH GROSS MARGIN AT 69%, REFLECTING STRONG PROFITABILITY FROM HIGH-VALUE AEROSPACE TOOLING & PRECISION MANUFACTURING

• H1 REVENUE GREW 85% YOY TO ₹231 CR, WHILE NET PROFIT INCREASED 71% TO ₹60 CR, WITH EBITDA MARGIN AT 38% & GROSS MARGIN AT 67%

• H1 REVENUE ALREADY REACHED APPROXIMATELY 96% OF FULL-YEAR FY26 REVENUE, WHILE H1 NET PROFIT REPRESENTED NEARLY 94% OF FY26 PROFIT

• ORDER BOOK SURGED 715% YOY TO ₹855 CR, PROVIDING STRONG MULTI-YEAR REVENUE VISIBILITY ACROSS AEROSPACE, PRECISION COMPONENTS & INDUSTRIAL MANUFACTURING

• APPROXIMATELY ₹589 CR OF ORDER VISIBILITY RELATES TO LONG-TERM CUSTOMER AGREEMENTS & AWARDS SPREAD OVER 5–10 YEARS, WITH EXECUTION DEPENDENT ON QUALIFICATIONS, CUSTOMER SCHEDULES & SERIAL PRODUCTION

• COMPANY SECURED A $7.5 MILLION FIVE-YEAR AEROSPACE COMPONENTS AGREEMENT WITH FACC, WITH POTENTIAL CONTRACT EXPANSION UNDER DISCUSSION

• COMPANY SECURED AN APPROXIMATELY $43 MILLION TEN-YEAR PROGRAM WITH A FRENCH AEROSPACE TIER-1 CUSTOMER FOR AIRCRAFT DOOR COMPONENTS, SUPPORTING LONG-TERM PRECISION COMPONENT GROWTH

• HONEYWELL AEROSPACE AGREEMENT COVERS ENGINE & CONTROL-SYSTEM COMPONENTS OVER 10 YEARS, WITH AN OPTION TO EXTEND BY AN ADDITIONAL TWO YEARS

• MORE THAN 250 PRECISION COMPONENT PARTS HAVE BEEN QUALIFIED, WITH OVER 340 ADDITIONAL PARTS IN THE PIPELINE, SUPPORTING A SIGNIFICANT EXPANSION IN SERIAL PRODUCTION OPPORTUNITIES

• SEMICONDUCTOR BUSINESS HAS ONE ESTABLISHED GLOBAL OEM CUSTOMER & TWO ADDITIONAL CUSTOMERS IN THE PIPELINE, WITH QUALIFICATION PROGRESS EXPECTED TO SUPPORT FUTURE REVENUE SCALE-UP

• HOBEL BELLOWS CONTRIBUTED APPROXIMATELY 30% OF H1 REVENUE, WITH DEMAND FROM DATA-CENTER GENERATORS, TURBINES, LOCOMOTIVES & INDUSTRIAL CUSTOMERS

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS AS9100 CERTIFICATION FOR THE VIZAG FACILITY BY FEBRUARY 2027, SUPPORTING HIGHER-VALUE AEROSPACE & PRECISION MANUFACTURING OPPORTUNITIES

• SAUDI ARABIA JV INVOLVES INITIAL EQUITY INVESTMENT OF APPROXIMATELY $4 MILLION, WITH COMMERCIAL MANUFACTURING READINESS TARGETED FOR MARCH–APRIL 2027 & INITIAL FOCUS ON OIL & GAS LOCALISATION

• NUCLEAR BUSINESS HAS QUALIFIED APPROXIMATELY 13–15 SYSTEMS & SUBASSEMBLIES, WITH POTENTIAL OPPORTUNITIES LINKED TO FOUR UPCOMING REACTOR PROJECTS

• COMPANY HOLDS APPROXIMATELY 27% EQUITY IN DEHYA ENGINEERING & EXCLUSIVE MANUFACTURING RIGHTS FOR PROPULSION ENGINES, WITH 20 KG, 40 KG, 50 KG & 100 KG THRUST VARIANTS UNDER DEVELOPMENT

GANDHAR OIL REFINERY Q2 CONCALL: RECORD REVENUE UP 73% YOY, EBITDA SURGES 337%, PAT JUMPS 368%, GROSS SPREADS HIT EXCEPTIONAL LEVELS & CAPACITY EXPANSION SUPPORTS GROWTH

• MANAGEMENT REMAINS OPTIMISTIC ABOUT SUSTAINING ELEVATED GROSS SPREADS DURING Q3–Q4 FY27, SUPPORTED BY BASE OIL SUPPLY CONSTRAINTS, DISCIPLINED SOURCING, STRONG PRICING & HEALTHY DOMESTIC DEMAND

• MANAGEMENT CONTINUES TO WORK TOWARD EARLIER FY27 VOLUME GROWTH GUIDANCE OF 8–11%, ALTHOUGH WEST ASIA GEOPOLITICAL DISRUPTIONS & WEAKER UAE EXPORT VOLUMES REMAIN KEY UNCERTAINTIES

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS STRONG PROCESS & INSULATING OILS DEMAND TO CONTINUE, DRIVEN BY TRANSFORMERS, POWER INFRASTRUCTURE, RUBBER INDUSTRIES & DATA-CENTER INVESTMENTS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS IMPROVED CAPACITY UTILISATION DURING Q3–Q4, SUPPORTED BY RECENT DEBOTTLENECKING, CAPACITY EXPANSION & HIGHER DOMESTIC PRODUCTION

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS TEXOL UAE EXPORT VOLUME RECOVERY AS WEST ASIA SHIPPING & RAW MATERIAL SUPPLY DISRUPTIONS EASE, WHILE HIGHER FREIGHT & INSURANCE COSTS ARE BEING PASSED ON TO CUSTOMERS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS LONG-TERM GROSS SPREADS TO MODERATE FROM CURRENT EXCEPTIONAL LEVELS AS SUPPLY CONDITIONS NORMALISE, BUT BELIEVES THEY COULD REMAIN ABOVE HISTORICAL ₹8,000–9,000/KL LEVELS

• Q2 REVENUE SURGED 73% YOY TO A RECORD ₹1,847 CR, WHILE EBITDA JUMPED 337% TO ₹288 CR & NET PROFIT INCREASED 368% TO ₹186 CR

• Q2 EBITDA MARGIN EXPANDED SHARPLY TO 15.6% VS 6.2% LAST YEAR, WHILE GROSS PROFIT REACHED ₹388 CR WITH GROSS MARGIN AT 21%

• Q2 GROSS SPREAD REACHED ₹29,128/KL, SUPPORTED BY ELEVATED SELLING PRICES, TIGHT BASE OIL SUPPLY & EFFICIENT PROCUREMENT

• CURRENT SELLING REALISATIONS INCREASED TO APPROXIMATELY ₹1.35 LAKH/KL VS ₹80,000/KL AT FY26-END, REFLECTING SIGNIFICANT PRICING IMPROVEMENT

• H1 REVENUE SURGED 82% YOY TO ₹3,579 CR, WHILE EBITDA REACHED ₹569 CR & NET PROFIT STOOD AT ₹392 CR

• H1 FY27 NET PROFIT WAS APPROXIMATELY 2.9 TIMES THE ENTIRE FY26 PROFIT, REFLECTING EXCEPTIONALLY STRONG MARGIN EXPANSION & EARNINGS GROWTH

• PROCESS & INSULATING OILS VOLUMES GREW 23% YOY IN H1, SUPPORTED BY STRONG DEMAND FROM POWER TRANSMISSION, TRANSFORMERS, INDUSTRIAL APPLICATIONS & DATA CENTERS

• PERSONAL CARE, HEALTHCARE & PERFORMANCE OILS VOLUMES REMAINED BROADLY FLAT IN H1, WITH WEAKER PERSONAL CARE DEMAND OFFSET BY STABLE HEALTHCARE & PHARMACEUTICAL REQUIREMENTS

• LUBRICANT VOLUMES REMAINED BROADLY STABLE YOY BUT INCREASED APPROXIMATELY 9% QOQ, WHILE STANDALONE BUSINESS VOLUMES GREW AROUND 16% YOY IN H1

• TOTAL INSTALLED CAPACITY REACHED APPROXIMATELY 8.39 LAKH KL, INCLUDING 6.02 LAKH KL IN INDIA & 2.36 LAKH KL AT TEXOL UAE, FOLLOWING APPROXIMATELY 2.40 LAKH KL OF CAPACITY ENHANCEMENTS

• INDIA CAPACITY UTILISATION STOOD AT APPROXIMATELY 82%, WHILE CONSOLIDATED UTILISATION WAS AROUND 61%, PROVIDING ADDITIONAL HEADROOM FOR VOLUME GROWTH

• OVERSEAS REVENUE INCLUDING TEXOL REACHED ₹1,721 CR IN H1, CONTRIBUTING APPROXIMATELY 48% OF CONSOLIDATED REVENUE, DESPITE EXPORT VOLUME DISRUPTIONS

• WEST ASIA CONFLICT & STRAIT OF HORMUZ DISRUPTIONS AFFECTED UAE RAW MATERIAL AVAILABILITY & EXPORT VOLUMES, WHILE SOUTH KOREAN SOURCING REMAINED STABLE & LIMITED GULF SUPPLIES RESUMED

• STANDALONE BUSINESS REMAINED DEBT-FREE, WHILE CONSOLIDATED BORROWINGS DECLINED TO ₹85 CR VS ₹168 CR IN MARCH 2026, WITH CASH BALANCES OF APPROXIMATELY ₹135 CR

• CONSOLIDATED H1 OPERATING CASH FLOW STOOD AT APPROXIMATELY ₹180 CR, WHILE RECEIVABLE DAYS INCREASED TO AROUND 70 VS 67 EARLIER

• SILVASSA UNIT 2 FLOODING RESULTED IN AN EXCEPTIONAL LOSS OF APPROXIMATELY ₹21 CR, WITH OPERATIONS RESUMED IN AUGUST & INSURANCE RECOVERY CLAIM SUBMITTED

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS QUARTERLY DEPRECIATION OF APPROXIMATELY ₹10–10.5 CR & SLIGHTLY LOWER INTEREST COSTS OVER THE NEXT TWO QUARTERS, WHILE FUTURE CAPEX IS EXPECTED TO BE FUNDED PRIMARILY THROUGH INTERNAL ACCRUALS

• MANAGEMENT REMAINS POSITIVE ON STRONG GROSS SPREADS, PIO DEMAND, DOMESTIC CAPACITY UTILISATION, HEALTHY CASH FLOW & LOW DEBT, BUT MARGIN NORMALISATION, WEST ASIA DISRUPTIONS, TEXOL EXPORT WEAKNESS & UNCERTAIN VOLUME RECOVERY REMAIN KEY RISKS

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS APPROXIMATELY ₹500 CR REVENUE OVER THE NEXT TWO YEARS, SUPPORTED BY MANUFACTURING CAPACITY EXPANSION, STRONGER DOREME BRAND PENETRATION, DIGITAL CHANNEL GROWTH & WIDER DISTRIBUTION

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS INFANTWEAR REVENUE CONTRIBUTION OF APPROXIMATELY 20% VS CURRENT 12–13%, SUPPORTED BY NEWBORN GIFT SETS, DEDICATED MANUFACTURING CAPACITY & PRODUCT INNOVATION
• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS WOVEN APPAREL CONTRIBUTION TO REACH APPROXIMATELY 10% OF REVENUE BY THE END OF NEXT YEAR, DRIVEN BY NEW NIGHTSUITS, PANTS & EXPANSION BEYOND EXISTING KNITTED PRODUCTS
• MANAGEMENT PLANS TO INCREASE ADVERTISING EXPENDITURE FROM APPROXIMATELY 2% OF REVENUE TO 3.5% BY FY27-END, SUPPORTING BRAND VISIBILITY, CUSTOMER ACQUISITION & ONLINE SALES GROWTH
• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS IMPROVED OPERATING LEVERAGE OVER THE NEXT TWO QUARTERS AS RECENTLY COMMISSIONED MANUFACTURING UNITS ACHIEVE HIGHER UTILISATION & EMPLOYEE PRODUCTIVITY

• Q2 NET PROFIT GREW 23.3% YOY TO ₹5.08 CR, WITH PAT MARGIN AT 8.2%, DESPITE HIGHER RAW MATERIAL COSTS, EMPLOYEE EXPENSES & OPERATING INVESTMENTS
• H1 REVENUE GREW 33.9% YOY, WHILE EBITDA REACHED ₹17.57 CR WITH MARGIN IMPROVING TO 16% VS 15.1% LAST YEAR
• H1 NET PROFIT INCREASED 34.7% YOY TO ₹9.09 CR, WITH PAT MARGIN AT 8.3%, REFLECTING HEALTHY REVENUE GROWTH & IMPROVED HALF-YEAR PROFITABILITY
• DIGITAL CHANNELS CURRENTLY CONTRIBUTE APPROXIMATELY 10% OF REVENUE, WITH AMAZON OPERATIONS RECENTLY STARTED, MYNTRA LAUNCH EXPECTED SHORTLY & QUICK-COMMERCE OPERATIONS INITIATED IN BENGALURU & HYDERABAD
• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS BETTER MARGINS FROM DIRECT-TO-CONSUMER SALES THROUGH DOREME.IN COMPARED WITH THIRD-PARTY MARKETPLACES, ALTHOUGH DIGITAL ADVERTISING COSTS REMAIN SIGNIFICANT
• NEW DEDICATED INFANTWEAR MANUFACTURING FACILITY HAS CAPACITY OF APPROXIMATELY 2,500 PIECES PER DAY, WITH EXPECTED ADDITIONAL ANNUAL REVENUE OF ₹3–4 CR
• COMPANY INTRODUCED FOUR-PIECE & SIX-PIECE NEWBORN GIFT SETS, WHILE A NEW IN-HOUSE EMBROIDERY UNIT USING JAPANESE MACHINERY SUPPORTS PRODUCT DIFFERENTIATION & VALUE ADDITION
• APPROXIMATELY 15% OF TOTAL REVENUE COMES FROM OUTSOURCED PRODUCTS, WHICH CARRY SLIGHTLY LOWER GROSS MARGINS COMPARED WITH IN-HOUSE MANUFACTURING
• MANAGEMENT HAS A LONG-TERM AMBITION TO EXPAND ITS DISTRIBUTION NETWORK TO APPROXIMATELY 300 DISTRIBUTORS & 20,000 RETAIL TOUCHPOINTS, SUPPORTING DEEPER PENETRATION ACROSS INDIA
• AVERAGE REVENUE PER DISTRIBUTOR STANDS AT APPROXIMATELY ₹80 LAKH, WHILE HEALTHY RETAIL STORE PRODUCTIVITY IS ESTIMATED AT ₹1,000/SQ. FT./MONTH WITH STORE-LEVEL EBITDA MARGINS OF 15–20%
• MANAGEMENT IS EVALUATING EXCLUSIVE BRAND OUTLET & FRANCHISE EXPANSION, WITH ESTIMATED STORE SETUP CAPEX OF ₹2,500–3,000/SQ. FT., ALTHOUGH NO FIRM STORE-OPENING TARGET HAS BEEN ANNOUNCED
• COMPANY IS EXPLORING INTERNATIONAL DISTRIBUTION OPPORTUNITIES IN THE MIDDLE EAST & AFRICA FOLLOWING PARTICIPATION IN THE SAUDI FASHION & TEXT EXPO, BUT NO FORMAL EXPORT REVENUE GUIDANCE HAS BEEN PROVIDED
• MANAGEMENT IS EVALUATING A NEW GREENFIELD MANUFACTURING PROJECT TO SUPPORT MEDIUM-TERM GROWTH, WITH FINAL CAPEX & FUNDING DECISIONS PENDING; INTERNAL ACCRUALS & DEBT REMAIN POTENTIAL FUNDING SOURCES
• MANAGEMENT REPORTED NO LONG-TERM DEBT AT THE TIME OF THE CALL, WHILE WORKING CAPITAL, INVENTORY BUILDUP & SHORT-TERM BORROWINGS REMAIN IMPORTANT MONITORABLES

**JIO PLATFORMS – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**NOMURA: INITIATE BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,340**
- Jio has evolved from a market disruptor into a market leader.
- Holds 42% of India's wireless subscribers, 60% of data traffic and 43% of home broadband.
- Expects the listing to support Jio's position as a tariff price-setter, enabling steady tariff hikes that competitors can follow.
- Estimates 13.5% EBITDA CAGR over FY26–FY29.
- Strong network and subscriber leadership support long-term value creation.
- Home broadband is expected to become the second major growth engine.
- Global technology licensing offers additional long-term growth potential.
- With most 5G capex largely completed, lower capex intensity could drive a sharp improvement in free cash flow.

**MOTILAL OSWAL (MOSL): INITIATE BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,350**
- Jio Platforms is India's largest digital connectivity platform, with Reliance Jio serving 533 million subscribers.
- Expects wireless revenue market share to increase by 100 bps to 43.3% by FY29.
- Forecasts Jio to account for 73% of incremental home broadband industry net additions over FY26–FY29.
- Digital growth opportunities include cloud, enterprise communications, IoT, managed services and international partnerships for 5G/UBR technology.
- Forecasts FY26–FY29 CAGR of:
  - Revenue: 14%
  - Reported EBITDA: 15%
  - PAT: 20%
- Growth drivers include subscriber additions, approximately 15% tariff hikes from March 2027, home broadband expansion and scaling digital platform offerings.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Both brokerages initiate coverage with Buy ratings, highlighting Jio's leadership, pricing power and digital ecosystem.
- Tariff hikes, home broadband growth and digital services are expected to drive earnings expansion.
- Lower 5G capex intensity could improve free cash flow and support future value creation.
- Target prices: ₹1,340 (Nomura) and ₹1,350 (MOSL).

**LARSEN & TOUBRO (L&T) – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹4,842**
- Q2 FY27 beat three of four guidance parameters: order inflows, execution and working capital; margins missed expectations.
- E&C execution increased 22% YoY despite Middle East disruptions, driven by 26% growth in the Middle East and 16% growth in India.
- Middle East order inflows rebounded strongly.
- Backlog reached US$90 billion, up 28% YoY, providing strong revenue visibility.
- FY27 guidance retained: 10–12% growth in new orders and execution, with flat margins.
- L&T has begun executing its FY31 strategy, expanding into AI, electronics manufacturing, green technology and chemicals.
- Won India's largest Nvidia AI factory order, supporting its AI infrastructure ambitions.

**MACQUARIE: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹4,710**
- Revenue grew 16% YoY and PAT increased 33% YoY.
- EBITDA remained broadly flat as margins declined 130 bps YoY to 8.7%, reflecting cost escalations.
- Record quarterly order intake and backlog growth of 28% each, led by international orders.
- Core order inflows grew 32% YoY.
- Management retained FY27 guidance despite Gulf-region challenges and improving private-sector participation in India's capex cycle.

**NOMURA: NEUTRAL | TARGET PRICE: ₹3,940**
- Execution and order inflows beat expectations, but margins disappointed.
- International execution was stronger than expected, while cost pressures persisted.
- H1 FY27 order inflows grew 22% YoY.
- FY27 order inflow growth guidance remains unchanged at 10–12%.
- Consolidated EBITDA was 7% below Nomura's estimate and 2% below consensus, despite 1% YoY growth.
- Valuation stands at 20.2x FY28 estimated EPS and 17.5x FY29 estimated EPS.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong execution, record order inflows and a US$90 billion backlog reinforce L&T's growth visibility.
- Margin compression from cost escalation remains the key near-term concern.
- AI, electronics manufacturing and green technology offer potential long-term growth opportunities.
- Brokerage views are largely positive: CLSA and Macquarie maintain Outperform ratings, while Nomura remains Neutral.
- Target prices: ₹4,842 (CLSA), ₹4,710 (Macquarie) and ₹3,940 (Nomura).

**MARUTI SUZUKI – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**HSBC: BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹14,500**
- Demand commentary remains strong, with management guiding for 10% domestic wholesale growth in H2 FY27.
- Margin recovery may be gradual as price hikes remain cautious.
- Margin improvement depends partly on a moderation in commodity costs.
- Valuations appear reasonable, with declining commodity prices identified as a key trigger.

**NOMURA: BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹13,046**
- Q2 FY27 performance was broadly in line with expectations.
- EBITDA margin stood at 8.9%, versus Nomura's estimate of 8.8%.
- Strong H2 FY27 guidance supports near-term demand visibility.
- Potential slowdown in FY28 remains a risk.
- Electric vehicle (EV) contribution is an important metric for the stock's performance.

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹14,537**
- Q2 EBITDA margin reached 8.9%, up 71 bps QoQ, ahead of consensus.
- Margin improvement was driven by cost-reduction measures, price hikes and the retail-wholesale gap.
- Management expects 10% domestic portfolio growth in H2 FY27, with exports broadly flat, implying overall volume growth of approximately 7–10%.
- CLSA remains conservative, factoring in 5% volume growth for H2 FY27.
- Inventory stood below normal at 17 days, while the order book reached 2.7 lakh units after Dussehra.
- Management remains confident of achieving its 10% domestic volume growth guidance.
- Commodity costs are expected to remain broadly flat QoQ in Q3 FY27, supporting a gradual EBITDA margin recovery.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong domestic demand, low inventory and a healthy order book support H2 FY27 volume growth.
- Margin recovery depends on cost control, pricing and commodity trends.
- FY28 demand sustainability and EV contribution remain important monitorables.
- All three brokerages are positive, with target prices ranging from ₹13,046 to ₹14,537.

MARKET DEVELOPMENTS – TWO CONTRASTING TRENDS

1. RBI – OVERSEAS CAPITAL FLOWS UNDER SCRUTINY
- Reports suggest tighter scrutiny of large overseas investments and capital outflows.
- This raises concerns for investors using overseas investment structures.
- However, enhanced scrutiny does not necessarily mean the automatic route has been abolished or all overseas investing is prohibited.

2. NIFTY ON-CHAIN CONTRACTS – 24×7 LEVERAGED TRADING
- Trade[XYZ] launched a synthetic Nifty 50 perpetual contract on Hyperliquid on October 27, 2026.
- Offers 24×7 trading with leverage of up to 20x.
- The contract provides synthetic index exposure, not ownership of Nifty 50 stocks.
- Its launch raises questions around regulatory jurisdiction, offshore derivatives access and legality for Indian residents.
- The launch should not be interpreted as SEBI approval.

3. TAXATION – MARKET SPECULATION
- Discussions around potential tax changes are circulating.
- Any proposed tax relief should be treated as speculation until officially announced.

4. COMMODITIES – POTENTIAL BENEFICIARY
- Commodity trading may attract greater speculative interest amid uncertainty in other markets.
- Higher trading volumes do not automatically translate into higher profitability for every participant.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- Overseas investment scrutiny and the emergence of 24×7 on-chain derivatives represent contrasting developments.
- Commodity markets could benefit from shifting trading activity, but this remains a thesis rather than a confirmed outcome.
- Await official clarification from regulators and exchanges before drawing firm conclusions.

- Annual production is targeted to scale up to 8 lakh tyres by 2030.
- A potential second phase includes a proposed 50:50 joint venture to establish a dedicated plant for high-value passenger car tyres.
- The proposed JV would target Indian and international markets.
- BKT will use its own technology for BKT-branded tyres, while Pirelli-branded tyres will be produced under the partnership arrangement.

Key Takeaway
- Partnership provides BKT an entry into the premium passenger car tyre segment and an opportunity to utilise its manufacturing capabilities.
- Production ramp-up and the potential JV could support long-term diversification beyond its traditional tyre businesses.
- Key monitorables: production commencement, capacity utilisation, investment requirements and profitability of the new segment.
- Impact: Positive – Long-Term Growth Opportunity

Operational Updates
- Strong volume growth driven by cement and GGBS demand across regions, supported by ramp-up in North India.

- Added 36 MW of wind capacity during the quarter.
- Total renewable capacity, including WHRS, reached 167 MW.

Capacity Expansion – Nagaur
- Commissioned a 1.0 MTPA grinding mill, taking grinding capacity to 3.5 MTPA; clinker capacity stands at 3.3 MTPA.

- Commissioned WHRS, OLBC and AFR co-processing systems to improve cost efficiency.

Shiva Cement Amalgamation
- Boards approved the amalgamation of listed subsidiary Shiva Cement into JSW Cement.
- Aims to create a unified cement platform and unlock operational, financial and management synergies.

- Transaction is subject to regulatory, shareholder, creditor and NCLT approvals.
- Completion expected in 12–14 months, subject to timely approvals.

- However, EBITDA growth lagged revenue growth in Q2, while H1 EBITDA declined 2% YoY, indicating margin pressure.
- Net debt of ₹4,287 Cr and the planned amalgamation remain important monitorables.
- Impact: Mixed to Positive

**ONE 97 COMMUNICATIONS (PAYTM) – GOLDMAN SACHS MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Goldman Sachs maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹2,010.
- Q2FY27 revenue grew 28% YoY (33% like-for-like), with further acceleration expected as UPI MDR revenue starts flowing in.
- EBITDA beat Goldman Sachs estimates by 10%, with continued margin expansion.
- UPI MDR could improve payment processing margins by 2.5 bps, potentially contributing ₹800–900 Cr to FY28 EBITDA.
- Financial services growth accelerated, supported by improving personal loan trends.
- Meaningful revenue and EBITDA contribution from postpaid is expected from FY28.
- Payments market share improved for another quarter, with strong monthly transacting user (MTU) additions.
- Higher-than-expected device-related capex may increase depreciation and amortisation costs, leading to some EPS estimate cuts.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong revenue growth, margin expansion and potential UPI MDR benefits support the outlook.
- Higher capex and resulting depreciation costs remain key concerns.
- Impact: **Positive**

**Brokerage Update**

- Citi maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹1,940.
- Q2 EBITDA and EBIT came 4% and 1% above Citi estimates at ₹270 Cr and ₹120 Cr, respectively.
- Net payment margin increased 0.5 bps QoQ to 9 bps, ahead of Citi's expectations.
- Financial services revenue growth accelerated to 49% YoY from 45% in Q1FY27.
- UPI-MDR is expected to add 2.5 bps to net payment margins, translating to around ₹900 Cr in FY28E.
- Higher DLG share in merchant lending may pressure near-term contribution margins.
- Financial services growth and net payment margins are improving, even excluding UPI-MDR.
- Paytm is increasing investments in AI, marketing, user acquisition and its on-ground sales network.

- Improving financial services growth and payment margins support the earnings outlook.
- Higher investments and DLG-related costs may weigh on near-term margins.

**MANKIND PHARMA – KOTAK MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Kotak maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹3,035.
- Q2FY27 performance was strong, driven by domestic formulations, BSV and international markets.
- Management expects to outperform IPM growth by 1.1–1.2x over the next two quarters.
- Base business recovery is visible through improving volume growth and a richer chronic-care product mix.
- BSV continues to deliver sustained growth momentum.
- OTC business remains the key concern, with growth yet to pick up.

Stock Fundamental in detail                            
@Fundamental3

**MANKIND PHARMA – JPMORGAN MAINTAINS NEUTRAL**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- JPMorgan maintains **Neutral** rating with a target price of ₹2,700.
- Q2 revenue came 3% above estimates, driven by strong India Rx and healthy export growth, offsetting consumer business weakness.
- India business grew around 16% YoY, partly supported by a low base.
- EBITDA margin stood at 27%, around 100 bps above estimates.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance remains unchanged at 25.5–26.5%.
- Consumer business growth guidance cut to single digits from high-single-digit to double-digit growth.
- Management expects double-digit consumer growth from next year, supported by e-commerce and quick-commerce channels.
- E-commerce and quick-commerce mix rose to around 18% in Q2 from 12% last year.
- EBITDA estimates raised by 3–4% on better visibility in India Rx and exports.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong India Rx, exports and margin performance supported the Q2 beat.
- Sustainable India outperformance and consumer business recovery remain key monitorables.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**MANKIND PHARMA – MACQUARIE MAINTAINS UNDERPERFORM**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Macquarie maintains **Underperform (U-P)** rating with a target price of ₹2,200.
- Q2 revenue, EBITDA and adjusted PAT beat estimates by 3%, 4% and 12%, respectively.
- EBITDA beat was driven by higher revenue, better gross margins, operating leverage and lower R&D expenses.
- PAT beat was supported by higher EBITDA, stronger other income and a slightly lower effective tax rate.
- BSV business remained strong across key brands.
- Consumer healthcare performance remained subdued due to weak category demand and softness in eastern and southern India.
- Net debt declined to ₹2,640 Cr from ₹3,380 Cr in June.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance remains at 25.5–26.5%, despite Q2 margin of 27.1%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong earnings beat and lower net debt support the financial position.
- Weak consumer healthcare performance remains a concern.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**MANKIND PHARMA – BERNSTEIN MAINTAINS UNDERWEIGHT**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Bernstein maintains **Underweight (UW)** rating with a target price of ₹2,057.
- Q2FY27 results offered limited evidence to justify the company's premium valuation.
- Domestic business grew 15.9%, with gastro and vitamins improving, while anti-infectives grew 5.4% and consumer healthcare just 1.2%.
- Volume growth stood at 6.7%, supported by seasonal acute demand and an easier GST-affected base.
- New brand contribution remained limited, raising concerns about the sustainability of headline growth.
- Consumer recovery has been delayed again, highlighting concerns around weakening momentum and slow brand creation.
- Exports performed better than expected, while BSV continued to show improved execution.
- Margins beat estimates, but management retained its 25% margin guidance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Domestic growth and exports offer support, but recovery remains uneven.
- Consumer weakness, limited new-brand traction and premium valuation remain key concerns.
- Impact: **Negative**

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
